minor.issue: When CIMITIR_TRUST_PROXY is unset, X-Forwarded-For CAN still change the per-IP bucket because uvicorn ships with proxy_headers=True and forwarded_allow_ips='127.0.0.1' by default — uvicorn rewrites request.client.host from XFF before FastAPI sees the request. On a fresh online server (port 8134, TRUST_PROXY unset) the 127.0.0.1 cerere bucket was correctly 429 after 20 calls, but a 21st POST with X-Forwarded-For: 9.9.9.9 returned 200 and created a new rl:cerere:9.9.9.9 bucket, i.e. an attacker on the loopback (reverse proxy, sidecar, container) can bypass the limit by rotating the header. The app-level TRUST_PROXY=0 guard is therefore not sufficient on its own. Suggested fix: launch uvicorn with --no-proxy-headers (or --forwarded-allow-ips='') unless CIMITIR_TRUST_PROXY=1, OR inside client_ip() read the raw peer from request.scope['client'] (uvicorn stores the real peer in scope, but modifies it before view code). The underlying behaviour is standard uvicorn, so documenting the deployment requirement + fronting with the correct flag is enough.

action_items: Decide how to prevent X-Forwarded-For from flipping the per-IP bucket when CIMITIR_TRUST_PROXY=0 (recommend starting uvicorn with --no-proxy-headers in that mode, or deriving client_ip from the ASGI scope's raw peer rather than request.client.host).

rca of the issue: X-Forwarded-For NOT resetting the limit was expected on 8134, but observed to reset. RCA: uvicorn starts with proxy_headers=True and forwarded_allow_ips='127.0.0.1' by default; because the TCP peer is loopback, uvicorn's ProxyHeadersMiddleware rewrites scope['client'] using the first XFF value BEFORE Starlette/FastAPI construct request.client. portal_ratelimit.client_ip() reads request.client.host, so it sees '9.9.9.9' and allocates a new per-IP bucket. CIMITIR_TRUST_PROXY=0 is honoured at app level but is defeated by the ASGI server. Mitigation: launch uvicorn with --no-proxy-headers when CIMITIR_TRUST_PROXY != '1', or compute the real peer from the raw transport.
